the concept of identity has been transformed in recent years by post structuralist and deconstructionist theories that have challenged the claims of the Cartesian subject; that Emmanuel Levinas' thought on identity and alterity is an important part of this debate and that it has been particularly influential on the concept of racial difference.
the concept of identity has been radically transformed over the past century, and that the work of Emmanuel Levinas is a significant contribution to that transformation.

Levinas is a major figure in the deconstruction of the Western philosophical tradition, and his critique of identity and his positive account of difference are both philosophically and ethically significant.

the following questions: How does Levinas describe identity and alterity in his thought?
the following questions: How is Levinas' account of the self in relationship with the Other an ethical one?

the way that the Levinasian account of the self and other can be used to develop a positive account of identity that does not depend upon a fixed and unchanging subject, but rather on a self in relation to an other.

Levinas has provided a powerful critique of the Western philosophical tradition, a positive account of the ethical relation to the Other and a reinsertion of Jewish thought and narrative into philosophy.
the Levinasian concept of alterity is a positive one, which is to say that it does not seek to deny the other's difference but rather to embrace and celebrate it.
Levinas' thought has been hugely influential, and that it is an influence which is still growing and expanding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Levinas' work is an attempt to articulate an ethical relation that is both a response to the Other and an expression of a self that has been transformed by that encounter.
the Levinasian approach to identity, alterity and difference is a radical critique of the Enlightenment subject and a revaluation of the ethical relationship between self and other.

The main takeaway from our work is that

Levinas' philosophy has the potential to provide a new and more inclusive understanding of identity and alteritiy, one that is not only ethical but also theological, a position that is both radical and conservative.
